reason: In moss descriptions, alar cells or a central strand that are 'not clearly differentiated' do not stand out from the cells around them. This is the same reading as 'indistinct' in the previous review. PATO:0002099 differentiated means a cell becoming specialized, which is a different sense.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values): orbicular PATO_0001934 + obovate PATO_0001936
reason: This is two shape values joined by a hyphen, a shape between orbicular and obovate. It needs the two-value pattern, not a new term. 'orbicularobovate' and 'obovatc' are transcription variants.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values): rhomboid PATO_0001938 + orbicular PATO_0001934 with value_qualifier sub (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md)
reason: This joins two shape values, and the second carries 'sub-'. Rhombic is already a rule to PATO:0001938 rhomboid, and suborbicular is orbicular plus the approximate-value qualifier.

'Bracts sheath-less' means the bract base does not form a sheath round the axis, which negates FLOPO:0991105 sheathing. The previous review rejected 'sheath' as a generic part, so an entity_absence rule is not possible.

A 'stigmatose' style carries stigmatic surface along part of its length, which is stigma tissue present on the style. Where the statement says 'upper 1/5' or 'above', that is the part of the bearer (docs/odp/04).
'Fleurs non épanouies' and 'leaflets not yet expanded' give a stage of development of the bearer, not a lasting quality. The statement's real quality applies to the bearer at that stage.

A trailer is a plant whose stems lie along the ground without rooting at the nodes, which is PATO:0000631 prostrate. FLOPO:0991009 creeping requires rooting at the nodes. In 'climber or trailer' the second value goes through the alternatives pattern.
'Short, tuft-like lateral branchlets' are branchlets crowded into close clusters from about one point. This matches FLOPO:0991098 fascicled, which covers branches.
This is a vague impression of the general look, not a defined quality. Where it means straggly habit, FLOPO:0991043 straggly already exists.
'Stems defoliate proximally' means the lower stem has lost its leaves: leaves absent, with 'proximally' as the part of the bearer. The inflorescence example ('defoliate axils') is a fragment.

label: flat-topped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's upper surface, or the tips of its parts, lying at about the same level, so that it has a flat top.
reason: This is a common term for inflorescences and capitula. PATO:0000407 flat would read as flattened, and PATO:0002455 corymb-like names a type of branching, not the outline. Sibling of PATO:0002455 corymb-like.

This is the negation of a moss-specific cell-wall term (walls thickened at the corners), and there is no positive term to negate. It occurs only in negated form in a few statements, so it is too thin to support a new class now.
In mosses, 'radiculose' means a stem covered with rhizoids (a felt of rhizoids). 'Not radiculose' therefore means rhizoids absent on the stem.

This means branched in a nearly pinnate way: branches on each side of a common axis, with 'sub-' as the approximate-value qualifier. 'Subpinnately to pinnately branched' is then a range between two values.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values): ovate FLOPO:0991024 + strap-shaped PATO_0002430
reason: This joins two shape values; lingulate is ligulate/strap-shaped (PATO:0002430, as in the 'ligulate' rule). No new term is needed.

This states a function, not a quality of form. The visible part of it (green stems) is a colour already covered by PATO. Examples like 'gorse has photosynthetic stem tissue' are prose rather than descriptions.

label: pseudautoicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte by virtue of its female plants bearing dwarf male plants, arising from spores, on their leaves or stems.
reason: A standard moss term for sexual condition, with no term in PATO or FLOPO. It is not under FLOPO:0991093 autoicous, because the male and female organs sit on separate individuals. Sibling of FLOPO:0991093 autoicous.
PO:0030124 corymb inflorescence has 'compound corymb' as a synonym. The word names the inflorescence, not a quality of it.

This is an ecological or physiological tolerance and needs an environmental second term. PATO:0000515 'tolerant to' is relational, and drought is not a plant part, so it is outside the part-plus-quality model of the floras. The examples are prose ('Mutton grass is...').

target: new: coloured marking (multi-colored PATO_0001533 with the colour of the marking, as for FLOPO:0991206 streaked)
reason: The statement gives a pattern of colour (marks) and the colour of the marks (red). Both have terms, but joining them needs a pattern; a term for every colour of marking would multiply without end.
This means slightly or nearly papillose. The 'sub-' is the approximate-value qualifier on FLOPO:0991059 papillose.

'Rachis terminé par une vrille' (leaf rachis ending in a tendril, as in legumes) means the rachis has a tendril: PO:0025366. For inflorescence axes or peduncles, PO has no tendril class, so those statements stay unannotated.
French 'unisexuées' and '1-sexuées' for flowers and inflorescences mean FLOPO:0991015 unisexual. Its definition already covers inflorescences that bear flowers of one sex.

'Fleurs/baies/piquants de taille variable' says that parts of one kind differ from one another in size. That is FLOPO:0991101 unequal. PATO 'increased variability of size' is a phenotype relative to a normal and does not fit.

label: campylotropous
definition: A curved quality inhering in an ovule or seed by virtue of the ovule's body being curved, so that the micropyle is brought close to the funicle and the embryo sac is bent.
reason: A standard botanical term for ovule form with no term in PATO or FLOPO. It is the first of the ovule-curvature series (orthotropous, anatropous, amphitropous) that could follow. Botany-specific.

Endocarp or fruit 'with a cavity' means having an empty space within: PATO:0002078 hollow. The examples are mixed: a disc 'with a central cavity' is a depression, and a seed with many filled cavities fits FLOPO:0991203 alveolate better.

label: achlorophyllous
definition: A color quality inhering in a plant or plant structure by virtue of its lacking chlorophyll, so that it is not green but white, yellowish, brown or reddish.
reason: A standard term for mycoheterotrophic and parasitic plants. PO has no chlorophyll or chloroplast to state as absent, and 'not green' does not say why. Botany-specific.
Junciform (rush-like) leaves and stems are long, slender and round in cross-section, so terete is the existing term. 'Junciform-subulate' is a two-value compound for the pattern.
French for grooved or furrowed. PATO:0002255 grooved (one or more channels) covers both one groove and many. '4-sillonné' is a count of grooves (docs/odp/03).

French 'soudées (entre elles)' for stamens, stipules and bracts means like parts fused together, which is FLOPO:0991067 connate (the same as the 'united' rule). Where the source says what they are fused to ('soudées à ...'), use FLOPO:0991129 adnate with the relation pattern (docs/odp/09).
